chapter: Gillespie and Carter on John Collins
title: Gillespie: his own piano voicings and why Collins should make a solo album
summary: Gillespie says he would play guitar like Collins, explains how he voices his arrangements, and wants Norman Granz to record Collins as a leader.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You know, I know a lot of the things that he does, the progressions because he was always -- he recognized the fact that I was sophisticated with progressions. I taught Miles progressions, Tad, showed Monk a lot of things and -- now don't -- I'm not saying that I didn't learn from all of them, you know what I mean, but I showed -- you see, I was always a piano player and I told him the other day, "Man, I always wanted to play a guitar". He said, "Nigger, you play enough piano". He said, "You should have been playing the guitar", because I would do the same thing, you see.

If I was playing the guitar, I'd be playing like John Collins because when I make an arrangement there is no set -- you know, like guys -- like Quincy and those guys have set things that they put in the arrangement. Now they just put that down by arrangement, you know, but me, I feel out every note, every chord, everything, you know.

The voicing, I figure out the voicing because I don't know how it's going to sound before. An arrangement on the piano, what sounds good on the piano doesn't sound good with instruments. So I have to make adjustments all the time. That's why I don't write because it takes me months to make an arrangement, a couple of months maybe to get it like I want it, you know.

I'll be scratching shit, you know, but that John Collins, I told him, I said, "Hey man," I said, "You know what you should do. You should make an album just with yourself because ain't nobody -- ain't no bass player could do it with you with the possible exception of Ray Brown that I know that's living now that would do a good job", with what John knows.
He would have to spend his time explaining. Ray has got some ears too. See John has got the ears. He's a bad cat.
He has never recorded a solo album or he has never recorded as a leader.
As a matter of fact, when I see Norman Grant, I'm going to tell Norman Grant that I want John Collins, that's true.

Since I've made one with Oscar -- I came out here and spent a week with him and we woodshedded -- just playing -- woodshed -- and stuck our heads together and make an album. It would be a hell of an album.
It would be a hell of an album because ain't nobody --
-- and the voicing that goes with it.
